features.text: Patient is 28 years old and female.
Patient experienced high blood pressure, light-headedness, and near-fall episode.
Patient's blood pressure was almost 200 in the ER.
Patient is taking lisinopril, which she has been on for a while.
Patient did not experience chest pain, palpitations, or visual disturbances.
Patient has no family history of hypertension, migraines, or neurological conditions.
Patient's blood pressure has been high once a month, usually when traveling for work and not eating as well.
Patient did not experience vision changes, speech difficulties, weakness, or numbness during the episode.
Patient does not have exact blood pressure reading from the ER, but it was very high, almost 200.
Patient does not have results from previous blood pressure monitoring or ambulatory measurements.
Patient does not have any other symptoms during these episodes besides light-headedness and feeling like she is going to fall.
Patient did not have any imaging studies like a head CT, MRI, or echocardiogram.
Patient does not have information about renal function tests like serum creatinine, eGFR, or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.
Patient had a headache during the episode, but no chest pain, palpitations, or visual changes.
Patient has not had any endocrine evaluations like plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio, cortisol levels, or adrenal imaging.
Patient's most recent physical examination showed slightly elevated blood pressure, a slight heart murmur, clear lungs, and trace pitting edema in lower extremities.
